title: Cabbage, Chinese, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Chinese cabbage (bok choy) is a leafy cruciferous vegetable. When boiled without added fat it retains a crisp texture and a mild, slightly sweet flavor. The vegetable is rich in vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber, making it a nutritious addition to meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bok choy is a staple in traditional Chinese cuisine, especially in soups and stir‑fries.
Its leaves and stems contain glucosinolates, compounds with potential anti‑cancer properties.
The plant grows quickly; a harvest is possible 30‑40 days after sowing.
Unlike regular cabbage, bok choy stems are tender and less bitter.
When stored in a sealed bag, bok choy stays fresh in the refrigerator for up to a week.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One cup of cooked Chinese cabbage provides over 70 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immune function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is involved in DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fibers aid digestion and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: 100 g of boiled bok choy contains about 15 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Glucosinolates can affect thyroid function when consumed in large amounts raw; cooking reduces this effect.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage.

items.title: Pesticide residue
items.content: When buying non‑organic produce, thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the cabbage to soups, stews, salads, or serve it as a side dish with fish or meat. Boiling without fat for 5‑7 minutes is enough to keep nutrients intact.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a perforated bag. Properly stored cooked cabbage remains good for 3‑4 days.
